text: hm well alright that is better. lets get to the main event here. i can finally see your shader paint bucket area and ai cant access it. but also it looks like hot shit if i have to be hoenst with you a painting tool that goes off of strings of text to identify them is not helpful at all, also why is so entirely decoupled from the actual color picker. i digress both are in a bad place. for starters. all this brush shit (and i said before but no one paid any attention) needs to move to the top toolbar when painting is in effect. i dont know a single damn ui where you reach to the bottom right to pick a brush its in a weird place and its also got some attrocious ux. buttons that are just literally pills of text are the bane of existence and also yeah i can go on and on. so the first move is clear. the brush selection and such it needs to be moved and thought about in a tasteful manner not just a quick goal t o satisify a request
resolution: Moved the brush controls out of the bottom-right Inspector dock (text-pill panel) to a contextual PaintToolbar that slides in under the menu bar while painting — the hybrid layout the user picked. Icon tools (fill/brush/pick) instead of pills; size + flow are inline sliders; the headline fix is a single unified 'ink' swatch that opens a popover with BOTH the color picker and the shader buckets rendered as live <Effect> THUMBNAILS (pick a material by seeing it, not reading a text string), plus a brush popover for shape presets + hardness/scatter. Split into the in-flow bar (PaintToolbar) and late-rendered PaintPopovers because this layout paints in tree order, so floating overlays must be late root children (same pattern as DropdownMenu) or they'd be occluded by the body; popover open-state is lifted to AppFrame. Removed ModelBrushDock from the Inspector. Cart-only, hot-reloads (transforms clean via esbuild); no rebuild needed for the toolbar (the separate AA brush fix fd3b1b9c2 still needs a framework rebuild). Sha 0fb53fa88. Known v1 rough edges to iterate on with the user: the color tab embeds the full ColorStudioWorkbench (its own redesign is parked), the ink popover opens left-aligned rather than under the swatch, and the shader tab renders many live Effect thumbnails at once (cheap since fill materials share a pipeline, but worth watching).
